parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
The exhaust systems of most modern gasoline-fuelled cars contain a catalytic converter with three metal catalysts.

These metals act as heterogeneous catalysts.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Name **three** metal catalysts used in catalytic converters.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a heterogeneous catalyst.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The exhaust systems of many diesel-fuelled cars contain an additional system to reduce vehicle emissions. This uses a liquid that is added to the exhaust system.

This liquid contains urea, $(\text{NH}_2)_2\text{CO}$, which decomposes on heating to isocyanic acid, $\text{HNCO}$, and ammonia.

reaction 1 $$ (\text{NH}_2)_2\text{CO} \rightarrow \text{HNCO} + \text{NH}_3 $$

Isocyanic acid reacts with water vapour to form ammonia and carbon dioxide.

reaction 2 $$ \text{HNCO}\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{NH}_3\text{(g)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} $$

Some values for standard enthalpy changes of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, and standard entropies, $S^{\ominus}$, are given in Table 5.1.

Table 5.1

| compound | $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | $S^{\ominus} / \text{J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{HNCO(g)}$ | -101.7 | +238.2 |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O(g)}$ | -241.8 | +188.8 |
| $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ | -45.9 | +192.8 |
| $\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ | -393.5 | +213.8 |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term entropy of a system.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data in Table 5.1 to calculate $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ for **reaction 2** at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$.
Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The ammonia formed in reactions 1 and 2 can be used to remove nitrogen dioxide from exhaust emissions, as shown.

reaction 3 $$ 8\text{NH}_3 + 6\text{NO}_2 \rightarrow 7\text{N}_2 + 12\text{H}_2\text{O} $$

Use the equations for reactions 1, 2 and 3 to construct an overall equation for the reduction of $\text{NO}_2$ by $(\text{NH}_2)_2\text{CO}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Isocyanic acid, $\text{HNCO}$, can form cyanuric acid, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_3\text{N}_3\text{O}_3$, under certain conditions.

$\text{C}_3\text{H}_3\text{N}_3\text{O}_3$ has a cyclic structure containing alternating carbon and nitrogen atoms in the ring system.

Suggest a structure for cyanuric acid.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
Isocyanic acid, $\text{HNCO}$, is a weak acid.

$$ \text{HNCO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_3\text{O}^{+} + \text{NCO}^{-} \quad \text{p}K_{\text{a}} = 3.70 \text{ at } 25^{\circ}\text{C} $$

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Write the mathematical expressions for $\text{p}K_{\text{a}}$ and $\text{pH}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the pH of $0.120\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HNCO(aq)}$.
Give your answer to **three** significant figures.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the percentage of $\text{HNCO}$ molecules that are ionised in $0.120\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HNCO}$.
